title: Level 5 (World Class) - B-19
notes:
West leads the ♣5 against 6♠. West's club lead is ruffed by South. A trump is played to the ♠A and another club is ruffed. West follows with a higher club than the one he led, marking him with 3 or more clubs. South cashes a trump honour. West discards and a diamond is thrown from dummy.

East has shown length in clubs in the bidding. When he shows up with 4 spades, it becomes quite likely that hearts are 5-1. If South plays carefully, he can succeed regardless of how hearts break and regardless of the position of the ♦K.

South should cash his other top trump, discarding the ♥4 from the dummy. South now plays on hearts for diamond discards. On the second round of hearts East discards (He cannot afford to ruff or he will be endplayed). South cashes dummy's remaining hearts, discarding diamonds. Again East must not ruff. A club is now ruffed.

If East has kept a diamond, South can cross to the ♦A and ruff North's last club for his twelfth trick. If East has discarded both of his diamonds on the hearts and the ♦K is still outstanding, South can later take the diamond finesse with confidence.
